item.title: MSWNet: A Deep Learning Fusion Framework for Municipal Solid Waste Detection From Optical and SAR Images
item.description: Transactions in GIS, Volume 30, Issue 6, September 2026.
item.dc:description: ABSTRACT Municipal solid waste (MSW), a global environmental concern whose monitoring is critical for environmental governance, can be effectively detected by remote sensing. Optical remote sensing is disturbed by weather, illumination, and vegetation, whereas synthetic aperture radar (SAR) data suffers from speckle noise and poor semantic characterization. Coupled with material heterogeneity, fuzzy boundaries, and spectral confusion in open‐pit MSW dumps, current single‐modal models cannot achieve accurate pixel‐level detection, hindering large‐scale automatic MSW mapping. Therefore, this study proposes MSWNet, a dual‐modal fusion deep network for high‐precision MSW detection, and builds the first pixel‐labeled MSW dataset of co‐registered optical‐SAR imagery. Specifically, to mitigate spectral confusion and material heterogeneity within MSW, a correlation‐guided cross‐modal fusion module is designed to adaptively weight optical‐SAR features, eliminate modal redundancy, and fuse discriminative multidimensional features for MSW‐background discrimination. Meanwhile, RefineNet, a lightweight residual edge refinement subnetwork deployed after the decoder, extracts edge details from upsampled coarse detection outputs to offset encoder downsampling‐induced edge loss and correct boundary misclassification for sharper MSW detection edges. Quantitative experiments demonstrate that the proposed MSWNet outperforms eight mainstream segmentation models with state‐of‐the‐art metrics (OA = 98.41%, Kappa = 0.9234, mIoU = 0.9277). This study can provide reliable technical references and fine spatial data for monitoring and intelligent management of open‐pit MSW.
item.content:encoded:
ABSTRACT

Municipal solid waste (MSW), a global environmental concern whose monitoring is critical for environmental governance, can be effectively detected by remote sensing. Optical remote sensing is disturbed by weather, illumination, and vegetation, whereas synthetic aperture radar (SAR) data suffers from speckle noise and poor semantic characterization. Coupled with material heterogeneity, fuzzy boundaries, and spectral confusion in open-pit MSW dumps, current single-modal models cannot achieve accurate pixel-level detection, hindering large-scale automatic MSW mapping. Therefore, this study proposes MSWNet, a dual-modal fusion deep network for high-precision MSW detection, and builds the first pixel-labeled MSW dataset of co-registered optical-SAR imagery. Specifically, to mitigate spectral confusion and material heterogeneity within MSW, a correlation-guided cross-modal fusion module is designed to adaptively weight optical-SAR features, eliminate modal redundancy, and fuse discriminative multidimensional features for MSW-background discrimination. Meanwhile, RefineNet, a lightweight residual edge refinement subnetwork deployed after the decoder, extracts edge details from upsampled coarse detection outputs to offset encoder downsampling-induced edge loss and correct boundary misclassification for sharper MSW detection edges. Quantitative experiments demonstrate that the proposed MSWNet outperforms eight mainstream segmentation models with state-of-the-art metrics (OA = 98.41%, Kappa = 0.9234, mIoU = 0.9277). This study can provide reliable technical references and fine spatial data for monitoring and intelligent management of open-pit MSW.
